terms.comment: A sentence of ours: we have found no set phrase for ordering “the same” in the authors searched or in Traupman, Morgan–Owens, or Levi–Bini. It is īdem with the dative, as when Nicobulus in Plautus answers mihi pār, idem est quod tibi, “it’s the same for me as for you” (Plaut. Bacch. 1109). Where the other person has just ordered, Mihi idem quod huic points to him.

phrases.latin: Idem mihi, quaesō, et puerō aquam.
phrases.english: The same for me, please, and water for the boy.
I’ll have the same as him.

phrases.latin: sed tū, quid tibist? — Pol mihi pār, idem est quod tibi.
phrases.english: But what’s the matter with you? — Lord, the same with me: it’s the same as with you.

sources: Lewis & Short: idem
